contract_reproduction.basis: R-01 through R-16 are present and mapped to exact PLAN sections, sole-roadmap increments, validation, and human gates. PLAN §§2, 9, 10.1, 14, 15, and 17 specify the install, ideation/research, decision, exact-digest READY, admission, execution, review, effect reconciliation, outcome, rollback, cleanup, release, export, and uninstall journey. The future Issue/CLI commands are explicitly unimplemented, identity-derived, typed, replay-safe, and paired with durable outcomes, waits, errors, and status/why views.

Protected Git, authenticated human issuance, approval custody, policy_admission_receipt_issuer, runtime validation, actuators, durable facts, external resources, and workers have separated authority. Delegation is limited to closed R0/R1 bounds after all human-needed predicates are false; R2-R4 and exception, canary, widening, promotion, UNKNOWN, cleanup-risk, and quiescence decisions remain exact-digest human decisions. Solo-owner independence-sensitive improvement stages remain disabled.

GitHub Issues and Projects are non-authoritative projections reconciled by versioned observation, signed plans, optimistic concurrency, operation-specific effects, readback, receipts, and UNKNOWN lookup rather than blind replay. Reviews bind exact head and expire on change. Auto-merge is off through Release 0 and the draft-PR pilot and can later cover only one earned closed R1 profile; protected categories and R2-R4 remain excluded.

Release 0 is one-owner/one-repository, read-only, restartable, exportable, and credential-free. Its hash-chained local journal has explicit tail-repair and interior-corruption behavior. Any external writer is blocked until Increment 3 proves PostgreSQL restricted roles, compare-and-append, outbox, database-time leases, restore/replay, and real two-session races. A second repository additionally waits for FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or stronger isolation, cross-repository substitution tests, and Increment 8 admission. PLAN §20 is the sole increment authority.

Consumer releases inventory and rehash every managed input/output, pin all executable references, emit verification/rollback receipts, and move through self-test, isolated dogfood, and opt-in rings. Tenant plus typed ScopeRef is immutable; every cross-boundary dependency type needs a dual-owner, field/port-limited, expiring and revocable envelope plus import receipt. GTM begins only after engineering admission as owned proposal/read-only research; publish, spend, and contact remain human-gated. The sandbox matrix, typed capabilities, signed context, narrow database roles, supply-chain controls, and break-glass non-waivable boundaries fail closed.

The A11-before-successor reclaim rule, immutable-terminal C11 remediation path, three DEEP-RESEARCH publication witnesses, rollback/cancellation partitions, deterministic exact-one canary child/link, unconditional EvidenceBundle denial, candidate-attributed PLAN prose, and current-heading-set validation are present in PLAN and/or the normative manifest. findings.title: The cleanup summary still reopens a terminal parent and the new remediation aggregate is missing from the durable catalog
findings.requirement: R-07 requires one unambiguous, safely implementable cleanup and retained-risk resurface path, with durable record ownership and authority defined consistently across the plan and incorporated manifest.
evidence: PLAN.md §13 says terminal Work, its parent aggregate, and its terminal CleanupItem are immutable; resurface/revocation/review-due uses C11 to atomically create or confirm a deterministic RemediationObligation and linked MAINTENANCE child while the parent remains historical terminal.

docs/state-transition-manifests.md §13 C11 stutters ESCALATED_DISPOSITION, creates the separate obligation/link/child absent-or-same, and says the historical disposed item remains terminal. Its following contract says C11 never changes parent Work, its cleanup coordinate, or its terminal CleanupItem.
PLAN.md §15 instead says the same eligible escalated disposition 'resurfaces the parent to CLEANING'. That is the exact reopening behavior the round-6 R6-AC-002 repair says was removed.

PLAN.md §5.1 calls itself the durable record catalog and its Effects and reconciliation family lists CleanupEscalationDisposition and quiescence records, but it does not list RemediationObligation or RemediationResurfaceReceipt. The newly required aggregate/receipt therefore lacks a catalogued owner, authoritative storage, and mutation rule even though §13 and the manifest require durable atomic creation.
findings.impact: A reader or implementer can follow §15 and illegally mutate terminal history, or follow C11 without a complete persistence/authority allocation for the obligation and receipt. The conflict reopens the previously confirmed cleanup safety defect and makes R-07 only partially closed at plan level.
findings.recommendation: Replace the final §15 clause with the exact immutable-parent C11 behavior. Add RemediationObligation, RemediationResurfaceReceipt, and RemediationClosureReceipt to the appropriate §5.1 durable-record family with the protected owner, authoritative store, append/transition role, absent-or-same transaction boundary, and resource-reuse block already required by manifest §13. Re-scan all cleanup summaries for parent reopening language.
findings.verification: No authoritative or explanatory current text permits FAILED/CANCELLED Work, its parent, or a terminal CleanupItem to return to CLEANING. The durable catalog names every C11-created or consumed record and assigns storage/mutation authority consistent with manifest §13; C11 replay/ownership/resource-block tests remain required future implementation gates.

findings.title: The current traceability file simultaneously says round-6 graph regeneration is pending and complete
findings.requirement: The plan-only package must state evidence/readiness status consistently so an owner can distinguish completed checkout-level repair from the still-pending fresh immutable retrieval, semantic review, implementation, model, and independent-closure gates.
evidence: requirements-traceability.md §6 says the current round-6 edit made the schema-3 graph stale and that 'regeneration is now pending'.
requirements-traceability.md §7 repeats that the current round-6 edit makes digest bindings 'stale pending combined evidence-prose repair and regeneration'.
requirements-traceability.md §9 says 'round-6 regeneration is pending' for the round-5 graph, then in the immediately following bullet says round-6 current-digest schema-3 regeneration is complete.

README.md and round-6-resolution.md say the graph is synchronized, matches current PLAN/manifest digests, and covers 27 headings. Direct recomputation confirms those current digests and exact 27-heading equality.
findings.impact: The named traceability/status artifact gives mutually exclusive readiness states. An owner cannot reliably tell whether the checkout-level regeneration prerequisite is done or still blocks review, and may confuse it with the genuinely pending future immutable same-run semantic gate.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite §§6-7 as dated historical statements that explicitly say the former staleness was repaired by the current round-6 regeneration. Replace §9's 'round-6 regeneration is pending' statement with the current synchronized status. Keep only fresh immutable retrieval, same-run semantic review, reviewed-edge regeneration, implementation/model gates, and independent closure pending.
findings.verification: README.md, PLAN §4/§24, requirements-traceability.md, round-6-resolution.md, and material-claims.json all distinguish the completed current-byte candidate-only regeneration from the pending fresh immutable reviewed-evidence run without any present-tense stale/pending contradiction.
